sentences.text: Mr. Saryati Dutta Ms. Sreemayee Roy ...for the Petitioners

The petitioners herein have assailed the proceeding being G.R. case no. 429 of 2017 arising out of Bidhannagar Police Station case no. 98 of 2017 dated 26.5.2017 under Sections 420/406/120B of the IPC, presently pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bidhannagar.

It is alleged in the complaint filed by way of Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure that the petitioners entered into a criminal conspiracy for cheating and misappropriation of the assets of the opposite party no. 2.

Since the year 2007, the petitioners had been supplying raw materials for construction work to the opposite party no. 2 for execution of projects in the State of Bihar and a total transaction account of Rs. 24,39,42,137/- had taken place between the petitioner no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2.
However, for facilitating the execution of the projects, various machines including crusher plant machinery and tippers were purchased and installed in the said project at Mizoram.
The opposite party no
. 2 was allegedly requested by the petitioners for selling the said machinery and tippers.
The complainant/opposite party no. 2 on the basis of long standing business relationship, agreed with such proposal and consideration price was fixed at Rs. 1.95 crores.

It is further alleged in the complaint that though the crusher machinery plant was given to the possession of the petitioners but no payment has been made to the opposite party no. 2 in spite of several requests.

Being aggrieved by the impugned proceeding, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners herein as complainant lodged a criminal case against the present complainant/opposite party herein with the allegation that despite supply of materials and confirmation of bills amounting to Rs. 2,80,71,136/- and despite the opposite party no. 2 herein have received a payment of Rs.
207.44 crores towards the work done from the Government, the said outstanding amount was not paid.
Accordingly, the opposite party no. 2 herein does not owe any amount of money from the petitioners herein.
He further submits that while this High Court granted anticipatory bail to the present petitioners clearly observed that the dispute between the parties is essentially a civil dispute.

He further submits that the proceeding under Sections 420 and 406 of the IPC cannot run concurrently in respect of the self- same cause of action.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners
, the application is admitted.

Petitioners are directed to serve a copy of the application upon the State through the office of the Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the opposite party no. 2 by speed post intimating the next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.

Learned counsel for the petitioners prays for interim stay of the impugned proceeding.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners and that the petitioners have made out an arguable case which requires adjudication on merit, let the impugned proceeding being G.R. case no. 429 of 2017 arising out of Bidhannagar North Police Station case no. 98 of 2017 dated 26.5.2017 under Sections 420/406/120B of the IPC, presently pending before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bidhannagar be stayed for a period of ten weeks or until further order, whichever is earlier.
Urgent Photostat certified copy of this order, duly applied for, be given to the parties upon compliance of all requisite formalities.
(Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
